newsitem.title: UK: Unilever has higher third quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Unilever has higher third quarter earnings.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc Friday posted a better-than-expected 5 percent rise in third-quarter profits.
The company announced that profits rose to 826 million pounds ($1.4 billion) for the quarter.
"I gritted myself for something rather unpleasant and it turned out very well," said David Lang, an analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
Unilever owns a range of household brands including Ponds, Persil and OMO washing detergents, Brooke Bond tea, and Walls and Igloo frozen foods.
The results beat analysts' forecasts which ranged from 760 million pounds ($1.25 billion) to 820 million ($1.34 billion).
"I think there is quite a lot of momentum in Unilever and that is before the benefits of management reorganisation which began in September," said Lang.
"The real strength came from the emerging markets of Latin America and Asia Pacific and the strong underlying performance in North America," said Unilever press officer Mike Haines.
"Although poor weather had a negative effect on ice-cream sales, other parts of the business in Europe did well," Haines said.

Despite the impact of a dull summer on ice-cream sales and profits, Unilever still managed to improve its profit by 13 million pounds ($21 million) to 502 million ($823.8 million) in the three month period from improved profits in detergents, frozen foods and personal products.
